wording: P47 states five mechanisms under which natural selection can favour cooperation, each a benefit-to-cost threshold: kin selection r > c/b, direct reciprocity w > c/b, indirect reciprocity q > c/b, network reciprocity b/c > k, group selection b/c > 1 + n/m; for reciprocity, Table 1 adds stricter thresholds for risk-dominance and advantageousness, and the latter links to the '1/3 rule', which P47 says holds in the limit of weak selection.
locator: P47 main text, Eqs. 1-5 and Table 1 (read in full)
counterevidence_limits: Author manuscript of a short review; each rule is derived in a simplified model, and P47's 1/3 rule is stated only for weak selection.
operationalization: FOR Allegiance = cooperation stabilised by a mechanism
verification_phrases: P47|Each rule can be expressed as the benefit-to-cost ratio of the altruistic act being greater than some critical value || P47|exceeds the cost-to-benefit ratio of the altruistic act: w > c / b || P47|This condition holds in the limit of weak selection

wording: Numerically solving P47's Table 1 matrices (w = q = r = 0.5, k = 4, n = 10, m = 20) reproduced every printed threshold exactly (ESS/RD/AD b/c = 2, 3, 4 for reciprocity). In a Moran process (N = 100, selection 0.005) the fixation probability of tit-for-tat in always-defect was below 1/N at b/c = 3.5 (0.00947) and above at 4.5 (0.01019), as the 1/3 rule predicts, but the crossing was at b/c 4.23, not within 5% of 4: the finite-N prediction is not supported at N = 100 (expected from the smoke test).
counterevidence_limits: The 1/3 rule is a large-N weak-selection limit; finite-N correction not sourced. Stochastic check at N = 20 matched the exact formula (0.0531 vs 0.0515).
